bull_thesis:
BULL THESIS — Terveystalo (TTALO.HE): "Own the best operator in Finnish private healthcare through a COVID-grade demand trough at a deep-value entry, and get paid twice — first when proven cost discipline holds the floor, then when post-cyclical revenue inflects in H2'26/2027 onto a structurally fatter margin base."

CORE LOGIC (probability-weighted): The probability that Terveystalo is a high-quality, durable franchise is very high (~90%) and rests on hard, management-disclosed, verifiable facts; the probability that the EQUITY works from here is more moderate (~55–60%) and is gated almost entirely on ONE variable — the timing of the Finnish demand recovery. The bull case is that the quality is so demonstrably real, and the margin floor so demonstrably defended, that you are underwriting a quality compounder bought at trough optics, where time is on your side and the inflection is a "when," not an "if."

1) THE MARGIN ENGINE IS REAL, VERIFIED, AND EXCEPTIONAL — THIS IS THE SINGLE STRONGEST FACT IN THE FILE. FY25 EBITA reached 14.0%, up from 12.8% in FY24 and 8.4% in FY22 — a 560bp expansion in three years. Critically, this beat management's OWN self-set target a full year early: the CFO's scorecard, in his words (Q4'25): "three years ago... we thought that we are brave when we say... 12% EBITA... Actually, we reached that one already 1 year ahead of time... and this year, '25, we are delivering 14%." When this management commits to a number whose levers are in its own hands, it has OVER-delivered, not missed. That is the highest grade of guidance credibility — a checkable, delivered hit, not a projection. The deep-value signal is therefore not a value trap on a melting business; it is a value entry on a business whose through-cycle earnings POWER has been structurally and permanently reset ~560bp higher than it was three years ago.

2) THE DOWNSIDE COST FLEX IS BEST-IN-CLASS AND WAS JUST STRESS-TESTED LIVE. In Q1'26 — the worst demand dip "since the start of COVID" — Healthcare Services volumes fell -11% and management flexed FTEs -10%, a near-1:1 cost-to-volume response. This held Q1'26 to the "third best... in absolute EBITDA or EBIT" (adjusted EBIT EUR 34M) despite everything except NPS going backwards. The bull point is decisive: the operating model works in REVERSE, cleanly. Most "operating leverage" stories are only ever demonstrated on the way up; Terveystalo just proved its cost machine on the way DOWN, in real time, in the worst environment in five years. This is the empirical floor under the equity — it caps how bad a "bottom called a fourth time" scenario can actually get for earnings, because management has shown it can shrink costs almost as fast as revenue falls.

3) THE WEAKNESS IS UNAMBIGUOUSLY MACRO, NOT FRANCHISE EROSION — AND THE EVIDENCE IS THE CUSTOMER, NOT THE NARRATIVE. Through the entire downturn, customer-quality metrics hit ALL-TIME HIGHS: appointment NPS 87.6 (Q4'25) rising to 88 (Q1'26); the medical-quality PEI indicator at all-time highs; "the most preferred brand... now... all-time high" and top-of-mind #1 for the first time (Q3'25). This is the crux of the bull case's quality leg: when a business loses revenue while simultaneously achieving record customer satisfaction and record brand preference, it is NOT losing share or losing relevance — it is a strong franchise whose end-market is temporarily cyclically depressed. You are buying a brand winner in a recession, not a structurally impaired asset. When Finnish macro turns, this NPS/brand strength is exactly the asset that captures the demand snap-back fastest.

4) "POST-CYCLICAL" IS A FALSIFIABLE PROMISE, NOT JUST AN EXCUSE — AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS IN THE BULL'S FAVOR. Management repeatedly labels healthcare services "post-cyclical" (Q4'25). The bear reads this as a built-in alibi. The bull reads it as a structurally grounded claim: occupational/private healthcare demand lags the macro DOWN (employers cut connected-employee headcount and discretionary care late) and therefore will lag the macro back UP. Management has now told the committee the bottom "has been passed" (Q1'26: "we are seeing a market bottoming out... the bottom has been passed", connected employees "as well, we see bottoming out"). If post-cyclicality is real, then a stabilizing-to-improving Finnish economy in late 2026 mechanically pulls Terveystalo's volumes positive into H2'26 and 2027 — onto the 14% margin base. The asymmetry: revenue stabilization on a 560bp-higher margin structure produces disproportionate EBIT and FCF, because the operating leverage that worked cleanly in reverse will work cleanly forward.

5) MANAGEMENT IS COUNTER-CYCLICALLY DEPLOYING CAPITAL FROM A POSITION OF STRENGTH — AND THE GROWTH IS SIGNED, NOT TALKED. This is not a company hunkering down and hoping. Funded by "dry powder" from the profitability program, it has: SIGNED the Hohde dental acquisition (Dec'25), explicitly to "double the dental business" toward a "double the profitability" goal; bolted on Pilke ophthalmology (Dec'25); committed a EUR 20M two-year occupational-health renewal program; and is actively pruning the portfolio (child-welfare divestment closed Jan'26; low-margin legacy outsourcing run off into a higher-margin residual — "remaining legacy contracts are on a higher end in the margin"). The Q3'25 M&A funnel was described as "all-time high activity... the funnel is there, and it's strongest that it has ever been during my term." The bull reads counter-cyclical buying correctly: management with the best balance sheet and the proven margin engine is acquiring scale and capability INTO the trough, when assets are cheapest — exactly what a high-quality compounder does. Hohde closing in Q3'26 is a near-term, datable catalyst: the first consolidated proof point of inorganic growth landing.

6) THE AI/DIGITAL OPTIONALITY HAS SHIPPED PRODUCT — IT IS NOT VAPORWARE, AND IT IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT MARGIN LEVER. The bear's strongest "buzzword" critique is partly disarmed by delivery: the MedHelp occupational platform is "live... used by the first paying customers" with "very positive" early feedback (Q1'26); Ella is launched and scaling; AI-assisted appointments are scaling. The bull's read of "project Nova" (the new Q1'26 back-office AI cost program) is not "they need more cost help because revenue won't come" — it is that management has identified a SECOND, structurally distinct efficiency vector (back-office automation) on top of the front-line one it already exhausted. Even the unscoped "Ella... some 30% efficiency improvement" (Q1'26), discounted heavily, points to a real productivity tailwind in the largest cost line (physician labor). The optionality: if even a fraction of the digital-health "10X" ambition and the three-modality architecture (physician-led via Ella; algorithm-led digital-health retail; insight-centric via MedHelp) lands, the through-cycle margin ceiling is HIGHER than the 14% already booked — meaning the bear's "margin is tapped out" claim has a credible offset that costs you nothing at the entry price.

7) THE TEAM IS TRANSPARENT AND STABLE — A RARE COMBINATION THAT LOWERS THE RISK PREMIUM. Every flattering optic was eventually CONCEDED under analyst pressure: the Q4'24 one-off CLA bonus that flattered the YoY improvement ("makes the improvement slightly better looking than it in real life is"); Sweden "not making proper profits yet"; the occupational-health damage being partly self-inflicted via pricing/billing; the repeated public-sector mis-forecast ("I've been... saying that now it opens up... and... it has not opened up"). This is the behavioral signature of a credible-but-promotional team, NOT an evasive one — and the CEO/CFO pair (Iho, Pajunen) is continuous across all three calls. For a capital allocator, candor + continuity = a lower probability of a nasty surprise and therefore a lower required risk premium on the deep-value entry.

KEY CONDITIONS THE BULL CASE REQUIRES (and how to monitor them):
(a) The H2'26 demand bottom must be approximately right THIS time. The first genuinely positive Healthcare Services VOLUME quarter and a turn in CONNECTED-EMPLOYEE numbers are the falsifying/confirming checkpoints. The bull does not need a V-shaped recovery — it needs revenue to STOP falling, after which the 14% margin and cost flex do the work.
(b) The margin floor must hold near 14% through continued volume softness — which Q1'26 (-10% FTE vs -11% volume holding EBIT to "third best Q1 ever") already demonstrated is achievable.
(c) Hohde must close (~Q3'26) and the EUR 20M occupational program must begin converting — the first tangible evidence the deferred growth is arriving, not evaporating.
(d) NPS/brand must STAY at all-time highs through the trough — confirming the franchise captures the eventual recovery rather than ceding it to Pihlajalinna/Mehiläinen.

SIZING LOGIC: Underwrite this as a quality operator you want to own THROUGH the trough at a deep-value price, with time on your side. The downside is buffered by a proven cost floor and a record-strong franchise; the upside is a post-cyclical revenue inflection landing on a structurally 560bp-fatter margin, plus shipped AI optionality and counter-cyclical M&A. The asymmetry favors accumulation on the demand weakness rather than waiting for an already-priced inflection. Prior conviction 4/Verdict B is defensible as a HOLD-and-accumulate on weakness — you are paid to be early in a name where the quality is verified and only the timing is in question.
bear_thesis:
BEAR THESIS — Terveystalo (TTALO.HE): "A genuinely excellent margin operator whose ONLY remaining lever is the one it does not control and has misjudged three quarters running. The cheap, controllable upside (efficiency) is — by management's own admission — exhausted; from here the entire thesis is a single, repeatedly-wrong macro call, narrated with an escalating AI gloss that is outrunning its disclosed results."

CORE LOGIC (probability-weighted): The bear case does NOT dispute the quality — it disputes the FORWARD return. The probability that the margin engine is real is ~90% (conceded). But the probability that the thesis from HERE depends on revenue rather than margin is ~100% — and management said so explicitly. And the probability that management's H2'26 demand-recovery timing is reliable is LOW, because it is the exact call they have now missed three consecutive quarters. The bear's quantified concern: you are buying a stock whose narrative spine ("revenue down / margin up") is, after three calls, hardening on the WRONG side — the revenue decline is ACCELERATING (Q1'26: "the market was even more negative than we expected... We have not seen this type of a dip since the start of COVID") while the margin offset is, by the CFO's own words, no longer available.

1) THE MARGIN LEVER IS TAPPED OUT — MANAGEMENT SAID SO ON THE RECORD, UNPROMPTED-THEN-CONFIRMED. This is the load-bearing bear fact, and it comes from the CFO directly under analyst pressure (Q4'25): asked if the improvement is sustainable quarter-by-quarter "like we did from Q4 '24 to Q4 '25? No, we can't." After an 8.4%→14% three-year run, the efficiency engine is mostly pulled. The brutal implication: a "deep value" thesis that worked for three years BECAUSE of margin self-help now has NO margin self-help left. From here, the thesis REQUIRES revenue — and revenue is precisely, and only, what is missing and deteriorating. The bull's "560bp-fatter base" is real but BACKWARD-looking; it is already in the FY25 print. The forward question is incremental, and the incremental margin lever is, by admission, gone.

2) THE TOP LINE IS FALLING ACROSS ALL THREE P&Ls AND THE DECLINE IS ACCELERATING — THIS IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM, AND IT IS GETTING WORSE. Q1'26: all segments "roughly minus 5% to minus 10% down"; "each and every number is negative... excluding the NPS"; the worst dip "since the start of COVID." The arc is the tell: the revenue-down motif HARDENED from "headwind" (Q3'25) to "the market was even more negative than we expected" (Q1'26). And when revenue falls faster than costs can be flexed, you get exactly what the CFO conceded in Q1'26 — "a drop through to our adjusted EBIT" as revenue outran the cost cuts. The bull's "third best Q1 ever in absolute terms" is expectation-management by re-anchoring: it is a defensible spin sitting on top of an admission that the trajectory went backwards on every line. Absolute-vs-relative framing is being deployed precisely BECAUSE the relative numbers are bad — the CFO himself: "in relative terms, we are absolutely disappointed" (Q1'26).

3) THE DEMAND "BOTTOM" HAS BEEN CALLED THREE QUARTERS RUNNING — THE FORECASTING RECORD ON THE ONE VARIABLE THAT NOW MATTERS IS DEMONSTRABLY POOR. Q3'25: public business "bottoming out", consumer "bottoming out." Q1'26: "the bottom has been passed", connected employees "bottoming out." The SAME bottom, re-called across three consecutive quarters on different line items, is itself evidence the trough has been deeper and longer than management projected — and is direct evidence their demand-timing judgment is unreliable. The CFO essentially confessed the public-sector miss (Q4'25): "I've been standing throughout the 3 years here quite many times saying that now it opens up. And at the same time, it has not opened up." The bear's central risk statement: the entire current thesis rests on an H2'26 turn that is the EXACT call management keeps getting wrong. You must explicitly underwrite the probability the "bottom" is called a FOURTH time — and there is no external corroboration offered for the H2'26 recovery; it is ASSERTED, not evidenced, and every assertion drew skeptical analyst follow-ups.

4) "POST-CYCLICAL" IS A SELF-SERVING, DOUBLE-EDGED ALIBI — IT MEANS THE RECOVERY LAGS EVEN IF MACRO TURNS NOW. The bear inverts the bull's favorite framing. Management calls healthcare services "post-cyclical" (Q4'25) — which is convenient cover for the current miss, but it ALSO means that even in the optimistic case where Finnish macro has already bottomed, Terveystalo's revenue lags the upturn. So the bull's "buy the inflection" is structurally LATE: the volume recovery, if post-cyclicality is real, arrives AFTER the macro recovery, pushing the actual earnings inflection further out than 2026 — consistent with management itself repeatedly deferring the real upside to "2027" (Q3'25: "clear attack plan for 2027"; Q4'25 closing reaches past the near term to "specifically '27"). The recurring deferral of upside to 2027 is the signal that 2026 is being managed internally as a write-off year. A deep-value buyer is therefore funding a potentially 18-month-plus dead-money window with no margin lever to bridge it.

5) THE GROWTH AVENUES THAT WERE SUPPOSED TO REPLACE MARGIN HAVE EITHER BEEN LOST OR ARE COOLING. (a) PUBLIC OUTSOURCING — touted as "opening" in Q3'25 — flipped to an EXPLICIT DOWNGRADE: Terveystalo LOST the flagship Pirkanmaa/Pirha tender to Pihlajalinna (Q3'25), and by Q1'26 management guides the book DOWN -EUR 20M in '26 toward a ~EUR 30M residual "continuing shrinking." A ~36% one-year revenue cut in a line is being narrated as "getting healthier" — the spin is outrunning the trajectory. (b) INSURANCE — a Q3'25 "growth driver" — was visibly downgraded in real time: an analyst literally color-coded it ("it went from dark green to lighter green"), and management's reframe slid from "growing steadily" (Q3) to "flattish... then the recovery in the second" (Q1). (c) OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH / connected employees — the core franchise — is DECLINING and the damage was partly SELF-INFLICTED: management conceded (Q1'26) the decline was triggered by its OWN two-step price increase plus "negative media coverage related to billing", the Alpha program's "unintended tail effects." A problem first narrated as cyclical was later admitted to be partly an own-goal. The bear synthesis: the "growth pivot" announced so forcefully in Q3'25 (Sweden "it's time to focus on growth"; Portfolio "Now, it's time to grow"; Healthcare Services "our eyes and focus turn into volume growth") has, within two quarters, round-tripped back to "adjust... scaled down... overhead... structures." The vocabulary round-trip from "grow" to "cut" in two quarters is the clearest hidden signal the growth pivot was announced PREMATURELY into a worsening tape.

6) "PROJECT NOVA" IS A TELL THAT MANAGEMENT PRIVATELY DOESN'T BELIEVE ITS OWN H2 RECOVERY. In Q4'25 management declared the operating model "as efficient as one can be" and "sustainable strong change." Then in Q1'26 it launched a BRAND-NEW back-office AI cost program — "project Nova... during next 12 months, you will hear more." Launching a fresh cost program AFTER declaring efficiency maxed out signals management expects to NEED more cost help — i.e., it does not fully trust the H2'26 revenue recovery to arrive on time. The bear's checkpoint: if "project Nova" and renewed cost actions quietly become the real 2026 earnings driver, then the "growth" story remains deferred and the stock is STILL just an efficiency play — but now one running on a second, smaller, less-certain efficiency vector after the big one is exhausted.

7) THE AI NARRATIVE IS THE PART GAINING THE MOST AIRTIME WHILE ITS DISCLOSED RESULTS LAG — A CLASSIC NARRATIVE-OUTRUNNING-NUMBERS PATTERN. The digital/AI story EXPANDS fastest across the arc (digital "10X" → three modalities → "project Nova"), yet it carries exactly ONE checkable headline metric — "Ella... some 30% efficiency improvement" (Q1'26) — with NO baseline, NO scope, NO denominator (which task? what share of physician workflow?). A precise-sounding, conveniently-round "30%" with no denominator is exactly what a forensic reader flags. The bear concern is not that the AI is fake (MedHelp has shipped); it is that the narrative AIRTIME devoted to AI is growing faster than the verifiable results, which is precisely how a promotional-but-credible team papers over a deteriorating core. Watch for a scope-defined restatement of the 30%; absent one, discount it to near-zero in the base case.

8) "IMPROVEMENT" OPTICS WERE FLATTERED AND ONLY CONCEDED UNDER PRESSURE — THE CLEAN UNDERLYING STEP IS SMALLER THAN REPORTED. The Q4'25 YoY improvement was partly an artifact of the prior-year EUR 500/employee CLA one-off bonus — the CFO admitted it "makes the improvement slightly better looking than it in real life is", but only AFTER an analyst pushed. Q4'25 also carried EUR 12.7M of adjustment items; Q1'26 EUR 7M ("slightly more than I would like to see"). Sweden is labelled a completed "turnaround" yet by management's own Q3'25 admission is "not making proper profits yet." The pattern: the headline always reads a notch better than the clean underlying reality, and the truth only emerges under questioning. A director should mechanically adjust headline "improvement" down for one-offs and absolute-vs-relative framing — which means the run-rate earnings base is somewhat softer than the trumpeted "all-time high" suggests.

9) CONTINUITY RISK AT THE DISCLOSURE SEAM, AT THE WORST POSSIBLE TIME. The long-tenured IR/Sustainability head (Kati Kaksonen, ~9 years) is departing as of Q1'26 — a continuity loss at the investor-facing seam precisely during a credibility-sensitive downturn. Minor on its own, but it removes a known quantity from the function that has, so far, been the channel through which management's candor was extracted. A checkpoint for whether disclosure QUALITY (the very thing the bull case leans on) is maintained.

WHAT WOULD CONFIRM THE BEAR (the falsification checkpoints):
(a) A FOURTH consecutive "bottoming out" with Healthcare Services VOLUME and CONNECTED-EMPLOYEE numbers still negative — confirming the demand-timing call is structurally unreliable and the dead-money window extends into 2027.
(b) Margin slipping materially below the 14% FY25 level as cost flex finally can't keep pace with continued volume declines (the Q1'26 "drop-through to EBIT" widening).
(c) "Project Nova" / renewed cost cuts becoming the actual 2026 earnings driver — proving "growth" is still deferred and this remains an efficiency story with the big lever already spent.
(d) Hohde close SLIPPING past Q3'26 on competition-authority remedies (management declined to comment on substance — "we don't comment the ongoing process from the content perspective"), removing the one near-term tangible growth proof point.
(e) The unscoped "30% Ella" figure never getting a scope-defined restatement — confirming the AI narrative is gloss, not P&L.
(f) NPS/brand finally cracking — which would convert a "macro, not share" story into genuine franchise erosion and break the bull's quality leg entirely.

NET BEAR VERDICT: This is a STABLE engine inside a DETERIORATING and ACCELERATING top-line cycle — net STABLE-to-deteriorating, NOT strengthening. The prior committee read (a clean "margin-fix → growth pivot") was correct on the margin fix but the growth pivot was announced INTO, and has STALLED IN, a worsening cycle. Prior conviction 4/B is NOT supported by anything strengthening. The honest framing: you are being asked to pay a deep-value price for a quality operator whose only forward lever is a macro call its own management has misjudged three times running, with the cheap controllable lever admittedly exhausted, the touted growth avenues lost or cooling, and an escalating AI narrative outrunning its disclosed numbers. The bear does not say AVOID the quality — it says do NOT size to an imminent or de-risked inflection, because the inflection is neither. At minimum this is hold-and-watch, not add; and if the fourth "bottom" prints negative, it is a value trap funded with a 14% margin that has nowhere left to go but flat or down.
consensus_delta:
DEEP-VALUE LENS, REGIME-OVERLAID (2026-06-05: late-cycle melt-up on an UNRESOLVED oil/inflation shock, WTI ~$92, CPI 3.8%, Fed/ECB higher-for-longer to ~Dec). The deep-value test reframes the question to: is the street pricing TERMINAL DECLINE into a company with stable/growing earnings POWER? The answer is SPLIT, and the regime is what tips the split decisively from 'watchlist' to 'pass.'

WHERE THE STREET IS RIGHT (no mispricing to harvest): The top line is in cyclical decline and ACCELERATING — Q1'26: all segments '-5% to -10% down,' the worst dip 'since the start of COVID.' That is not a mispricing; it is a fact management volunteered, and the regime makes it WORSE, not better. The single variable the entire forward thesis now rests on — a Finnish/Nordic discretionary-and-occupational-healthcare DEMAND recovery in H2'26 — is precisely the variable that an unresolved European energy/inflation shock and higher-for-longer ECB policy work AGAINST. Employers cut connected-employee headcount and consumers defer discretionary care exactly when real incomes are squeezed by a $92 oil print and sticky 3.8%-type inflation. So the street's 'revenue keeps falling' read is not just defensible — the regime raises the probability it is correct through end-2026.

WHERE THE STREET IS PLAUSIBLY WRONG (the real but UNHARVESTABLE delta): The through-cycle earnings POWER has been structurally reset — FY25 EBITA 14.0% vs 8.4% in FY22, a verified, target-beaten-a-year-early 560bp expansion — and customer metrics are at ALL-TIME HIGHS through the trough (NPS 87.6→88, PEI all-time high, #1 brand preference for the first time). Record NPS + record brand preference WHILE revenue falls is the cleanest possible falsification of a share-loss / structural-impairment thesis: this is a brand winner in a recession, not an eroding asset. A consensus that prices this as a melting wellbeing-county roll-up (the reflexive comp after the reform and the Pirha tender loss) IS pricing terminal decline into a durable franchise. THAT is a genuine consensus delta on the QUALITY axis.

WHY THE DELTA DOES NOT EARN CAPITAL IN THIS REGIME: The expectations arbitrage is two-sided and the bear half is equally FACT-GROUNDED — and the regime neutralizes the bull half's timing edge entirely. The incremental margin lever that drove the whole three-year re-rating is, by the CFO's own unprompted-then-confirmed admission (Q4'25), EXHAUSTED: 'improve QoQ like we did from Q4 24 to Q4 25? No, we can't.' That hands the forward thesis ENTIRELY to demand timing — the one variable management has missed 0-for-3 AND the one the regime specifically penalizes. The mispricing, if it exists, is a 12-24 month quality-compounder discount, NOT a 3-9 month catalyst gap — and in a fully-invested melt-up (BofA FMS cash 3.9%, Mag-7 ~30% of index), a no-catalyst, macro-demand-dependent, thin-coverage Nordic small-cap with falling revenue and an admittedly-spent margin lever is exactly the kind of slow-burn quality discount that has no forcing function to close on the relevant horizon and no mechanical buyer to defend it. The street is not 'looking the wrong way' in a way I can monetize before the macro itself turns — and the regime says do not pre-pay for a macro turn that needs a benign late-cycle that is not on offer.
forcing_function:
REGIME-PENALIZED. There is NO single hard-dated corporate event that, by itself, SHATTERS the consensus and forces a clean re-rating — and under the 2026-06-05 regime that scarcity is DISQUALIFYING for an allocation, not merely a reason to wait. The regime explicitly REWARDS a hard-dated catalyst INSIDE the H1/mid-2026 window and PENALIZES any thesis that needs a macro/rate rescue or whose catalyst is out-of-window or two-sided. TTALO fails all three sub-tests.

THE DEEP-VALUE RE-RATING CATALYSTS THE FRAMEWORK PRIZES ARE ABSENT: no buyback authorization flagged, no activist on the register, no value-crystallizing asset sale (the only 'sale' is the already-closed small child-welfare divestment plus the deliberate runoff of legacy outsourcing — a MANAGED DECLINE, not a crystallization), and no dividend-initiation or special-distribution catalyst. The regime-favored special-sit lanes (distressed/deleveraging, spinoff, forced-seller) are not present.

WHAT EXISTS ARE EARNINGS-PRINT CHECKPOINTS — and the regime turns them from 'wait for it' into 'penalize it': (1) PRIMARY: the H2'26 VOLUME print — Q2'26 (~August 2026) and Q3'26 (~October 2026), where the market finally sees whether Healthcare Services VOLUME and CONNECTED-EMPLOYEES turn POSITIVE for the first time. This is the only window the entire thesis hinges on, and it is (a) AT/JUST-PAST the edge of the mid-2026 window the regime rewards — Aug-Oct is later than the H1/mid-2026 catalysts the regime prizes; (b) genuinely TWO-SIDED — it can break the thesis as easily as confirm it; and (c) the EXACT call management has missed three times. Decisively, the positive outcome REQUIRES a benign Finnish/Nordic demand recovery — i.e., it effectively needs the macro NOT to deteriorate further, which is precisely the 'thesis that needs a rate/macro rescue' the regime tells me to PENALIZE. Front-running a thrice-missed, two-sided, out-of-window macro print, in a regime whose central tail (energy shock + higher-for-longer) works against that print, is not an edge — it is a coin flip with a quality skin, mispriced for the regime. (2) SECONDARY: HOHDE CLOSE, guided 'rather Q3 than Q4' 2026, pending competition-authority clearance — the only datable CORPORATE event, and a modest one: closing crystallizes the first consolidated proof of the growth pivot; slippage reads as a second deferral. Too small to shatter consensus alone, and itself out at Q3'26. (3) TERTIARY: a scope-defined restatement of the unscoped 'Ella 30%' claim — marginal either way.

RESOLUTION-DRIVER INDEPENDENCE (a regime priority): TTALO has ONE point of genuine independence worth crediting — its payoff is NOT directly levered to the regime's shared crowd factors (oil, AI-capex, Mag-7 concentration); it is a domestic Finnish healthcare name. But its catalyst is NOT independent of the regime's CENTRAL tail: higher-for-longer European rates and an imported-energy/inflation shock directly suppress the employer-headcount and discretionary-care demand the recovery needs. So the forcing function shares the dominant risk factor of the regime, in the wrong direction. SYNTHESIS OF TIMING: the re-rating is gated on a TWO-SIDED earnings print in the Aug-Oct 2026 window — later than the regime's rewarded window, on the exact variable the regime penalizes, repeatedly mis-timed by management, with no hard corporate catalyst of guaranteed date and direction to front-run. The regime-aware verdict is to STAND ASIDE: re-engage ONLY if the Q2/Q3'26 volume print actually turns positive (thesis de-risked, macro headwind disproven) OR a fourth negative print / broader risk-off unwind produces a genuine capitulation that resets price to a margin of safety that pays for owning the trough into 2027.
valley_of_death:
REGIME-DEEPENED. The 3-9 month window (Q2'26 reported ~Aug'26 through Q1'27 ~Feb'27) is a SLOW-BLEED dead-money trench with one binary that can crack the floor — and the 2026-06-05 regime widens the trench and raises the probability the floor is tested.

WHAT IS NOT HERE (and why that REMOVES the clean entry): The file shows NO debt-maturity wall, NO covenant stress, NO cash-burn hump, NO dividend-cut mechanic. To the contrary, management funds COUNTER-CYCLICAL M&A (Hohde, Pilke) and a EUR 20M occupational program from 'dry powder' — a 14% EBITA business with 1:1 cost flex generates cash even in the trough. That ABSENCE matters: it removes the sharp, datable, balance-sheet-manufactured washout a CRO normally waits to buy into. There is no 'flush' the company itself will produce.

WHAT THE REGIME MAKES WORSE: (1) THE FOURTH-MISS PROBABILITY RISES. The base case must weight a FOURTH consecutive 'bottoming out' that still prints NEGATIVE on Healthcare Services VOLUME and CONNECTED-EMPLOYEES (Q2'26 ~Aug, Q3'26 ~Oct). Management is 0-for-3 and Q1'26 admitted the market was 'even MORE negative than we expected.' The regime's unresolved oil/inflation shock and higher-for-longer European rates are a direct, ongoing headwind to exactly the employer-headcount and discretionary-care demand the recovery requires — so the probability the trough is deeper-and-longer-still is HIGHER under this regime than under a benign-disinflation base case. Each negative print compounds the credibility discount on the H2'26 promise and pushes the real inflection toward 2027, the horizon to which management has already, tellingly, deferred the upside. (2) THE 14% FLOOR — THE ONLY DOWNSIDE BUFFER — IS NOW EXPOSED TO A MACRO TAIL. Q1'26 already showed 'a drop through to our adjusted EBIT' as revenue outran cost cuts, AND the CFO has said the margin lever cannot improve further. # Forensic Dossier — Terveystalo Oyj (TTALO.HE)

**Coverage window:** Three consecutive calls — Q3 2025 (2025-10-23), Q4 / Full-Year 2025 (2026-02-13), Q1 2026 (2026-04-24).
**Company:** Finland's largest private healthcare-services group; three reporting P&Ls — Healthcare Services (largest), Portfolio Businesses (dental, public outsourcing), and Sweden (turnaround).
**Prior committee state:** Conviction 4 / Verdict B (deep_value signal). Prior dossier read this as a credible "margin-fixing → growth pivot."
**Evidence-base note (read this first):** The screener supplied **no structured financials panel** — the `metrics_str` field for this name is empty (`{"sector": ""}`). There is therefore **no independent quarter-over-quarter numbers grid to triangulate against**, and no externally-supplied earnings-beat rate. What follows is built from (a) the hard figures management itself put on the screen in the three calls, (b) management's own *backward references* to the multi-year trajectory (the 8.4%→14% EBITA journey, the Alpha profitability program, the connected-employee peak in '22–'23), and (c) the forward guidance and program targets debated live with analysts. This is a genuine **three-call arc** — unusual richness for an EU semi-annual-style reporter — so a real tone/credibility *slope* can be drawn. Where the conventional structured-financials cross-check is not supportable, I say so rather than fabricate a number. Every figure cited below is sourced to one of these three transcripts and attributed to the quarter.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across these three calls the core story is remarkably stable in *structure* but undergoes a clear and important shift in *posture* — from "we have fixed profitability, now we turn to growth" (Q3'25) to "the market got worse than we thought, so we are defending the margin engine while we wait for the cycle to turn" (Q1'26). The skeleton is identical each quarter; the confidence with which the "growth" half of the skeleton is delivered erodes meaningfully.

- **The spine is unchanged all three quarters: "improving profitability against a declining top line."** Q3'25: *"this quarter 3 was a quarter of margin improvement amid a revenue headwind."* Q4'25: *"the big headline here is profitability and efficiency ... all-time high profitability ... declining revenue due to macro."* Q1'26: *"the relative numbers are big. We see negative on everything else, excluding the NPS."* The revenue-down / margin-up motif is the one constant, and it hardens from "headwind" (Q3) to *"the market was even more negative than we expected"* (Q1).

- **The "now it's time to grow" promise is introduced forcefully in Q3'25, peaks in Q4'25, and is materially walked back in Q1'26.** In Q3 Iho repeats a near-liturgical refrain across all three P&Ls — Sweden: *"it's time to focus on growth"*; Portfolio Businesses: *"Now, it's time to grow"*; Healthcare Services: *"our eyes and focus turn into volume growth."* By Q1'26 the same segments are described as *"roughly minus 5% to minus 10% down"* and the growth language is conditional: *"market will not give — even though it starts gradually improving, it will not give anything for free."* The pivot-to-growth thesis was announced into a deteriorating, not improving, tape.

- **"Bottoming out" is the load-bearing forward claim — and it is repeated so insistently it becomes the tell.** Q3'25: public business *"bottoming out"*; consumer *"bottoming out."* Q1'26: *"we are seeing a market bottoming out ... the bottom has been passed"*, and connected employees *"as well, we see bottoming out."* The same "bottom" has now been called across three consecutive quarters covering different line items. A director should note that *the bottom keeps being re-called*, which is itself evidence the trough has been deeper and longer than management projected.

- **The digital/AI narrative is the one element that genuinely EXPANDS across the arc — and it expands fast.** In Q3'25 it is framed broadly: *"scaling up the digital health 10x"*, Ella *"launched"* as a UI. By Q4'25 it is formalized into a **three-modality architecture** (physician-led integrated care via Ella; algorithm-led "digital health retail" with AI-assisted appointments; insight-centric proactive care via MedHelp). By Q1'26 it carries a hard, checkable productivity claim — Ella delivering *"some 30% efficiency improvement"* — plus two named live products (MedHelp occupational platform live with *"first paying customers"*; AI-assisted appointments scaling) and a new back-office AI program, *"project Nova."* The AI story is the part of the narrative gaining the most airtime and specificity quarter over quarter.

- **Growth drivers introduced, sequenced, and partly delivered:** dental (named Q3 as a growth segment → **Hohde acquisition signed** by Q4 → reframed Q1 as *"a sort of a light or positive glimpse"* and the one segment with *"fairly good"* market conditions); Kela 65 / seniors (consistent positive across all three); insurance (Q3 *"growth driver"* → Q4 analyst flags the growth rate *"went from dark green to lighter green"* → Q1 *"flattish ... then the recovery in the second [half]"*). The insurance driver visibly *cools* across the arc.

- **Growth drivers quietly DE-emphasized:** public-sector outsourcing. In Q3 it is an active opportunity (*"opening public market"*, *"increased activity"* in tenders). But Terveystalo **lost the flagship Pirkanmaa/Pirha tender to Pihlajalinna** (disclosed Q3), and by Q1'26 management is openly managing the legacy book *down* — *"EUR 20 million reduction in the outsourcing portfolio revenues in '26"* with the remaining ~EUR 30M *"continuing shrinking year-on-year."* What was a growth avenue in Q3 is, by Q1, an explicitly *shrinking legacy* line that management is reframing as margin-accretive runoff.

**Net:** the core story has *contracted* in near-term ambition (the confident "time to grow" of Q3'25 has become "the cycle is very negative, look beyond it" by Q1'26) while *expanding* in one dimension — the digital/AI efficiency narrative. The thesis has migrated from **"profitability fixed → growth now"** to **"profitability engine proven under stress → growth deferred to H2'26/2027, bridge it with AI-driven efficiency."**

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

There is no external financials block, so the discipline here is to test management's narrative against (a) the hard figures management itself disclosed in these three calls and (b) internal consistency across the arc — does the spin outrun the arithmetic management volunteered?

|---|---|---|
| *"All-time high profitability ... best results ever"* (Q4'25) | FY25 EBITA **14.0%**, up from 12.8% FY24 and 8.4% FY22; the CFO: *"by '25, we will reach 12% EBITA. Actually, we reached that one already 1 year ahead of time ... and this year, '25, we are delivering 14%"* | **Fully corroborated and the single strongest fact in the dossier.** A 560bp EBITA-margin expansion over three years, beating their own 12%/FY25 target a full year early, is a verifiable, management-disclosed delivery — not a projection. The efficiency claim is real. |

| *"We have delivered the profitability turnaround"* in Portfolio Businesses and Sweden (Q4'25) | All three P&Ls described as *"improving with declining revenue"*; Sweden *"improved the profitability ... against very difficult market"* but *"not making proper profits yet"* (Q3) | **Mostly corroborated, with a Sweden caveat.** Group and Portfolio turnaround is credible; Sweden's turnaround is **profitability-direction, not profitability-level** — by management's own Q3 admission it is still *not* generating *"proper profits."* The word "turnaround" is doing slightly more work than the Sweden P&L has earned. |
| *"Sustainable strong change in our operating model ... as efficient as one can be"* (Q4'25) | But under direct analyst questioning the CFO concedes the Q4 YoY improvement was flattered: *"In Q4 '24, we had ... the onetime bonuses ... that one makes the improvement slightly better looking than it in real life is"* | **Diverges from the headline.** The same call that trumpets "all-time high profitability" also admits the Q4-on-Q4 *improvement* was partly an artifact of a prior-year one-off (the EUR 500/employee CLA bonus). The *level* is real; the *rate of improvement* was overstated by the optics until an analyst pushed. |

EUR 1M child-welfare divestment) | **Mixed — the absolute frame is true; the trajectory frame is poor.** "Third best Q1 ever in absolute terms" is a defensible spin, but it sits on top of an admission that *everything except NPS went backwards* and that there was *"a drop through to our adjusted EBIT"* as revenue fell faster than costs could be cut. The absolute-vs-relative framing is being used to soften a clearly disappointing quarter. |

But note: this is *defensive* efficiency (shrinking to match falling demand), not the *growth* operating leverage management had promised would materialize. |
| *"Hohde ... we are really delivering on growth"* (Q4'25) | Hohde signed Dec'25; closing *"expected to happen on the second half ... rather in Q3 than in Q4"* (Q1'26); EUR 20M occupational-health program; Pilke (ophthalmology) bolt-on Dec'25 | **Partially corroborated — direction yes, delivery still pending.** The M&A *is* real and signed, but as of Q1'26 Hohde is **not yet closed** (awaiting competition-authority clearance) and the EUR 20M program is mid-flight with returns explicitly deferred (*"once the market turns ... we are stronger than ever"*). The "delivering on growth" claim is contracted-but-not-yet-consolidated growth. |
| *"Ella ... some 30% efficiency improvement"* (Q1'26) | Single point estimate, no baseline, no scope (which task / what share of physician workflow) disclosed | **Unverifiable as stated.** A precise-sounding "30%" with no denominator is exactly the kind of figure a forensic reader flags — it may be real and task-specific, but it is uncorroborated and conveniently round. Monitor for a scope-defined restatement. |
| Outsourcing reframed as healthy runoff: *"remaining legacy contracts are on a higher end in the margin"* (Q1'26) | FY25 outsourcing revenue ~EUR 55M → guided −EUR 20M in '26 → ~EUR 30M residual *"continuing shrinking"* | **The spin outruns the trajectory.** A ~36% one-year revenue cut in a line, reframed as *"getting healthier,"* is a defensible margin argument but a clear top-line *negative* being narrated as a positive. After losing the Pirha tender, the "opening public market" growth story of Q3 has quietly become a managed decline. |

**Forensic synthesis:** The narrative is **strongly corroborated where it concerns the margin/efficiency engine — that part is real, verifiable, and genuinely best-in-class (14% EBITA, 1:1 cost flex).** It is **modestly *richer* than the numbers justify on the growth and "improvement" claims:** the Q4 improvement was partly a one-off optic (conceded under pressure), Sweden is not yet profitable at the level the word "turnaround" implies, the headline M&A is signed-not-closed, the flagship public tender was lost, and the "30% Ella" figure is unscoped. Crucially, **every divergence above was *eventually* conceded by management when an analyst pushed** — nothing was concealed outright — which is the behavioral signature of a credible-but-promotional team rather than an evasive one.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Trajectory rating: DECLINING (offensive→defensive shift), from a high base — confidence in the *engine* stays high and steady; confidence in the *near-term top line* falls hard across the three calls.**

- **Q3'25 — peak offensive confidence.** The language is growth-forward and almost swaggering on M&A: *"the activity on our desk is way higher than it has been for 5 years or so ... This is sort of an all-time high activity ... the funnel is there, and it's strongest that it has ever been during my term."* The agenda is framed as *"9 out of 10 moving very fast to the positive territory,"* with occupational health the lone problem child. This is a management team that believes the turn is imminent.

- **Q4'25 — confident on results, beginning to brace on the market.** The CFO's victory lap is unmistakable — *"three years ago ... we thought that we are brave when we say ... 12% EBITA ... this year, '25, we are delivering 14%"* — but the macro caveats multiply: *"we are living in a market, which is not favorable,"* *"revenue headwinds,"* *"the revenue was under pressure in all segments."* Iho's closing is still forward-leaning but now reaches past the near term: *"looking positively forward into H2 this year and specifically '27."* The pivot of the optimism *out to 2027* is the first clear defensive tell.

- **Q1'26 — defensive, with visible disappointment surfacing through the spin.** The tonal break is sharp. CFO: *"in relative terms, we are absolutely disappointed."* CEO: *"the market was even more negative than we expected ... We have not seen this type of a dip since the start of COVID."* The vocabulary has flipped from "grow / funnel / all-time-high activity" to *"adjust ... scaled down ... lower demand ... overhead ... structures ... a cycle is a cycle."* The single most-repeated forward word is no longer "growth" but *"bottomed out."* Confidence in the controllable engine remains intact (*"no matter how you view it ... we have been able to adjust"*), but confidence in demand has collapsed to "we think the worst has passed."

- **Guidance specificity actually IMPROVES even as tone darkens** — a credibility positive amid the gloom. Q1'26 is the most numerically forthcoming call: the EUR 34M EBIT, the −11%/−10% volume/FTE flex, the EUR 55M→EUR 30M outsourcing bridge, the EUR 20M reduction guide, the EUR 7M adjustment-item breakdown, the Hohde *"Q3 rather than Q4"* timing. Management does **not** retreat into vague "macro uncertainty" — when the news is bad they quantify it, which is the opposite of the evasive pattern.

- **A notable confidence asymmetry:** management is *most* confident precisely where it has hard delivered evidence (the margin engine, NPS at 87.6→88) and *least* confident — yet still insistent — where it is forecasting a turn it has now mis-timed three quarters running (the demand "bottom"). The honest read is a team that has earned the right to be believed on operations and *not yet* on its repeated near-term demand calls.

**Verdict on tone:** Declining trajectory, but a *high-quality* decline — the deterioration is in the macro environment and management's openly-conceded mis-forecasting of its depth, not in candor or operational grip. The shift from offensive (growth/M&A/funnel) to defensive (adjust/overhead/cost/cycle) language across the three calls is unambiguous and is the most important tonal fact for the director.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability score: MEDIUM (high on what they control, low on what they forecast).**

The structured earnings-beat rate was not supplied, so this is assessed on the internal track record visible across the three calls — and that record splits cleanly into two very different stories.

- **On the multi-year profitability target, credibility is HIGH and demonstrated.** The CFO's own scorecard is the best evidence in the dossier: a 12%/FY25 EBITA target set in 2022 was *"reached ... already 1 year ahead of time"* (12.8% in FY24) and then beaten to **14% in FY25** (Q4'25). When management commits to an efficiency/margin number with levers in its own hands, it has over-delivered. That is a strong, checkable hit.

- **On near-term demand/market calls, credibility is LOW and repeatedly missed.** Three consecutive quarters of "bottoming out" that kept being re-called is, on its face, a poor forecasting record:
  - Q3'25: Sweden *"the market seems to be picking up ... Sweden economy is doing better next year"*; public *"developing positively"* over the next 12 months.
  - Q1'26 reality: *"the market was even more negative than we expected going into the year ... we have not seen this type of a dip since the start of COVID."*
  The CFO essentially confesses the public-sector miss: *"I've been standing throughout the 3 years here quite many times saying that now it opens up. And at the same time, it has not opened up"* (Q4'25). Management's demand timing has been wrong, directionally and repeatedly.

- **There IS a soft sandbagging / optics pattern around adjustment items and absolute-vs-relative framing.** Q4'25 carried **EUR 12.7M** of adjustment items (*"majority ... related on our efficiency actions"*); Q1'26 carried **EUR 7M** (*"slightly more than I would like to see"*). The CFO openly conceded the Q4'24 one-off bonuses made the YoY improvement *"slightly better looking than it in real life is"* — i.e., the *clean* underlying improvement is smaller than the reported step. And the persistent "third best quarter ever in *absolute* terms" framing for a quarter where *"each and every number is negative"* (Q1'26) is expectation-management by re-anchoring. None of this is deceptive — it is all disclosed — but a director should adjust headline "improvement" optics down for one-offs and for the absolute-vs-relative framing.

- **Forward guide that IS quantified and trackable (good):** EUR 20M outsourcing-revenue reduction in '26 (*"we are very clearly going towards that one"*); Hohde close in Q3'26; EUR 20M occupational-health program over two years; group-level "growth deferred to H2'26 and 2027." These are concrete checkpoints — the H2'26 demand recovery is the one the whole thesis now rests on, and it is the very call management has missed three times.

**Reconciliation:** With no supplied beat-rate, I weight management's own two-sided record. The proven over-delivery on the controllable margin target prevents a Low score; the thrice-missed demand-timing call and the conceded one-off optics prevent a High score. **MEDIUM** — believe them on efficiency and cost flex; discount their H2'26 demand-recovery timing until a quarter actually prints positive volume.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

The Q&A pressure is concentrated on three recurring themes, and management's handling ranges from genuinely transparent to artfully deflected.

- **"Is the Healthcare Services margin sustainable, or is it a one-off-flattered peak?"** — the most forensically important exchange (Q4'25, Inderes/webcast). The CFO gave an unusually honest two-part answer: *"Is the improvement sustainable, meaning that can we improve quarter-by-quarter ... like we did from Q4 '24 to Q4 '25? No, we can't"* — because of the prior-year one-off bonuses — but *"on absolute level ... we have a huge operating leverage."* This is the pressure point where management is **most credible**: asked directly, they conceded the YoY *rate* was flattered and rested the bull case on absolute operating leverage instead. Watch this: the admission that they *cannot* keep improving the margin YoY caps the efficiency upside — from here, the thesis *requires revenue*, which is precisely what is missing.

- **Connected employees in occupational health — pushed every quarter, and it kept being bad news.** Analysts (and IR-fed webcast questions) returned to this in all three calls. Q3'25: management says it *"will not be ... turned around in 1 quarter ... a couple of quarters to get to ... all-time highs."* Q1'26: still declining, now *"stable throughout the quarter"* and projected to turn *"into positive going into H2."* The Q1'26 confession is the key disclosure: the decline was self-inflicted — *"that ... latter price increase, coupled with the negative media coverage related to billing was a negative trigger point for sort of many companies and additional tendering ... we saw the damage last year."* This is a topic analysts pushed on for quarters that **management initially framed as cyclical and only later admitted was partly a self-inflicted pricing/reputation own-goal** (the Alpha-program *"unintended tail effects"*). The forensic tell: a problem first attributed to "the market" was eventually conceded to be partly management's doing.

- **Public-sector outsourcing — repeatedly probed, repeatedly deferred, and it turned negative.** Analysts kept asking when the public market "opens up." Management's answer degraded from *"increased activity ... developing positively"* (Q3) to the CFO's near-apology *"I've been ... saying that now it opens up ... and ... it has not opened up ... the predictability makes it a bit difficult"* (Q4) and finally to *"the difficulty with public sector is to predict it"* plus an explicit −EUR 20M revenue guide (Q1). On the Pirha loss specifically, management deflected gracefully into a compliment — *"congrats to Pihlajalinna for good competition and a nice win"* — and reframed the loss as not-that-profitable-anyway (*"would have not been ... the richest agreement"*). A topic analysts pressed on as upside became a quantified downside.

- **Hohde closing/remedies (Q1'26, SEB) — a partial, content-light non-answer by design.** Asked about competition-authority remedies and timing, the CFO declined on substance — *"we don't comment the ongoing process from the content perspective"* — but gave a directional steer that the deal perimeter is *"rather on slightly more positive than we thought going in"* (Iho). Reasonable for a live regulatory process, but the director should note the close is **not yet certain** and is a flagged checkpoint for H2'26.

- **What analysts worry about that management is under-addressing:** the *timing and existence* of the demand recovery the entire thesis now hinges on. Every "bottomed out / H2 recovery" assertion is met with skeptical follow-ups, and management's only defense is its (mis-timed) judgment plus internal funnel/win-rate color. There is no external corroboration offered for the H2'26 turn — it is asserted, not evidenced.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **The terminology pivot from "fix" to "grow" — and then the silent retreat back to "adjust."** Q3–Q4'25 management ritualistically declares profitability *"done and dusted"* and growth the new priority. By Q1'26 the operative verbs are *"adjust ... scaled down ... overhead ... structures."* The vocabulary round-trip — from "grow" back to "cut" within two quarters — is the clearest hidden signal that the growth pivot was announced prematurely and the company has quietly re-entered defense.

- **"Project Nova" — a *new* cost program introduced in Q1'26, a tell that efficiency is being re-tapped.** *"We have a separate program related to applying AI in the back-office functions ... project Nova ... during next 12 months, you will hear more."* Launching a fresh back-office cost program *after* declaring the operating model *"as efficient as one can be"* (Q4'25) signals management privately expects to need more cost help — i.e., it does not fully believe its own H2 revenue recovery will arrive on time.

- **Competitive framing toward the public sector softened from "compete and win" to "polarizing and unpredictable."** Q3: actively bidding, congratulating the winner as a near-peer. Q1: *"wellbeing counties are polarizing ... there are those ... willing to take progressive measures ... and ... those ones who are still very cautious ... how that dynamic plays out is simply difficult to predict."* The shift from competitive confidence to "this is outside our control and unpredictable" is management distancing the thesis from a channel it can no longer time.

- **Insurance growth visibly downgraded in real time** — an analyst literally color-coded it (*"it went from dark green to lighter green"*, Q1'26). Management's reframe — *"it's not growing fast. It's growing steadily"* (Q3) → *"flattish ... then the recovery in the second"* (Q1) — is a quiet demotion of what was a Q3 *"growth driver."* The biggest moves are now pushed to *"2027"* (Q3'25: *"clear attack plan for 2027"*) — the recurring deferral of upside to 2027 is itself a signal that 2026 is being managed as a write-off year.

- **The "dry powder" phrasing recurs** (Q3 and Q1) — management repeatedly emphasizes balance-sheet capacity to invest/acquire. Combined with *"all-time high"* M&A funnel (Q3) and the Hohde/Pilke signings, this is management positioning for *counter-cyclical M&A* — buying into the trough. Forensically that is rational capital allocation, but it also confirms management expects the trough to persist long enough that buying now is attractive.

- **Management/continuity change at the IR seam.** Kati Kaksonen — IR and Sustainability head for *"almost 9 years"* — announces Q1'26 is her last quarter, closing with an unusually personal vote of confidence: *"I believe that Terveystalo will come through as a winner from this cycle."* The CEO/CFO duo (Iho, Pajunen) is stable and continuous across all three calls, which is reassuring; but losing a long-tenured IR lead during a credibility-sensitive downturn is a minor continuity risk and a checkpoint for whether disclosure quality is maintained.

- **"Post-cyclical" is deployed as a built-in excuse and a built-in promise.** Management repeatedly labels healthcare services *"post-cyclical"* (Q4'25) — which simultaneously explains why revenue lags the macro down *and* pre-commits the narrative that it will lag the macro back up. It is a double-edged framing: convenient cover for the current miss, but also a falsifiable promise the director can hold them to when Finnish macro improves.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE engine inside a DETERIORATING top-line cycle — net read: STABLE-to-deteriorating, NOT strengthening.**

Terveystalo is a genuinely high-quality operator caught in a deep, longer-than-forecast demand trough. The bull case is real and verifiable: a 560bp three-year EBITA-margin expansion to 14% (target beaten a year early), best-in-class downside cost flex (−10% FTE against −11% volume), all-time-high customer quality (NPS 88) confirming the weakness is macro rather than share loss, and disciplined counter-cyclical capital allocation (Hohde, Pilke, child-welfare divestment, legacy-outsourcing runoff into higher-margin residual). Management is transparent — every flattering optic was conceded under questioning — and the CEO/CFO pair is stable.

**But the trajectory across these three calls is a clear de-rating of the *growth* half of the thesis.** Revenue is falling in all three P&Ls and *accelerated* downward into Q1'26 (the worst dip *"since the start of COVID"*); the margin lever is, by management's own admission, largely exhausted (*"can we improve ... like we did ...? No, we can't"*); the flagship public-outsourcing growth avenue was lost (Pirha) and reframed as managed decline; the core occupational-health franchise suffered partly self-inflicted damage; and the demand "bottom" has now been called three quarters running. The prior committee read — a clean "margin-fix → growth pivot" — was correct on the margin fix but **the growth pivot has been announced into, and stalled by, a worsening cycle.** Prior conviction 4/B is not supported by *strengthening*; this is a hold-and-watch, not an add, until a quarter actually prints stabilizing-to-positive volume.

**The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing:** *The entire forward case now rests on one repeatedly-missed call — the H2 2026 demand recovery — because the margin engine is admittedly tapped out and revenue is the only remaining lever.* Management has over-delivered on everything it controls and mis-timed the demand turn three times. **Size the position to the risk that the "bottom" is called a fourth time** — i.e., underwrite this as a quality operator you want to own *through* the trough at a deep-value entry, not as a name where the inflection is imminent or de-risked. The first hard checkpoints are: (1) the next print of *connected-employee* numbers and Healthcare Services *volume* — the first genuinely positive volume quarter validates or breaks the H2'26 thesis; (2) the **Hohde close** (guided Q3'26) as the first consolidated proof of the growth pivot; and (3) whether *"project Nova"* and renewed cost actions quietly become the real 2026 earnings driver — if so, the "growth" story is still deferred and the stock remains an efficiency play, not a growth one.
